parts.problemMd: Explain **one** benefit for a business from the introduction of total quality management (TQM).
parts.solutionMd:
TQM makes every employee in the business responsible for quality at every stage of production **[1 mark]**, which means problems and defects are identified and corrected earlier in the process before more materials and labour are wasted **[1 mark]**, reducing the overall cost of production and lowering the number of faulty products that need to be scrapped or returned by customers **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a valid benefit of TQM. 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the benefit, for a maximum of 3 marks.
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Introducing TQM can improve the motivation of workers by making them feel that their contribution to quality is valued and important **[1 mark]**. When employees take ownership of quality in their own area of work, they are likely to feel more engaged and take greater pride in what they produce **[1 mark]**, leading to higher productivity and a better quality product overall, which helps the business to build a stronger reputation with its customers **[1 mark]**
> - TQM helps a business to build a culture of continuous improvement throughout the whole organisation **[1 mark]**, as all workers are encouraged to look for ways to improve the quality of what they do rather than leaving this responsibility to a separate quality control team **[1 mark]**, meaning the business is more likely to deliver consistently high-quality  products over time, helping it to retain customers and compete more effectively **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response.
> 
> Answers that list three benefits of TQM with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark.
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone.

parts.problemMd:
> **[case-study]**
> *Huawei *is a leading global provider of information and communications technology, infrastructure and smart devices. In March 2011, over one million of its C8500 smartphones were sold in China following its launch.
> 
> It now manufactures a wide variety of different products including *Huawei *smartphones, watches and tablets. In recent years *Huawei *has won many awards. In 2018 it was named the 68th most valuable brand by Best Global Brands. In 2019 it introduced a smartphone which had new photographic technology.

Analyse why *Huawei *would want good quality control when producing its smartphones.
parts.solutionMd:
Good quality control is important to Huawei because it is a leading global brand that has won many awards and has worked hard to build its reputation **[1 mark]**. If faulty smartphones reach customers, negative reviews and media coverage could seriously damage Huawei's image **[1 mark]**, which would be very harmful for a business named one of the world's most valuable brands in 2018 and competing against well-established global rivals **[1 mark]**

Good quality control is also essential because Huawei produces smartphones with complex new technology, such as the photographic innovations introduced in 2019 **[1 mark]**. If these advanced features do not work correctly, Huawei could face costly product recalls and refunds **[1 mark]**, which would significantly increase its costs and reduce the profit it makes on each device sold **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying points about why Huawei would want good quality control.
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the points to Huawei's context.
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the importance of quality control to the business.
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Huawei sold over one million C8500 smartphones in China in a single month **[1 mark]**. If a quality problem affected even a small percentage of these devices, the number of returns and refunds could be enormous **[1 mark]**, resulting in huge financial costs and a significant loss of revenue that would damage Huawei's performance as a global business **[1 mark]**
> - Good quality control helps Huawei to build and maintain customer loyalty in a very competitive global smartphone market **[1 mark]**. Customers who are satisfied with the quality of their Huawei device are more likely to buy another Huawei product when they next upgrade **[1 mark]**, helping Huawei to retain its existing customers and grow its market share against rivals who also produce high-quality devices **[1 mark]**
> 
> Answers that list six points about quality control with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark.
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone.

parts.problemMd: Explain **one** disadvantage to a business of using Total Quality Management (TQM).
parts.solutionMd:
TQM requires significant investment in training all employees to take responsibility for quality **[1 mark]**, which increases the business's costs and diverts resources away from other activities such as production or marketing **[1 mark]**, meaning the business may struggle to remain profitable in the short term, especially if it is a small business with limited financial resources **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a valid disadvantage of TQM. 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the disadvantage, for a maximum of 3 marks.
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Implementing TQM can be very time-consuming as it requires changing the culture of the entire organisation **[1 mark]**, which may slow down decision-making and reduce productivity while employees adapt to new processes and responsibilities **[1 mark]**, potentially causing the business to fall behind competitors who can operate more efficiently during this period **[1 mark]**
> - TQM relies on the commitment of every employee in the business to maintaining quality standards **[1 mark]**, but if some workers are resistant to change or lack motivation, the system may not work effectively **[1 mark]**, leading to inconsistent quality and wasted investment in a programme that fails to deliver the expected improvements **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response.
> 
> Answers that list three disadvantages of TQM with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark.
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone.

parts.problemMd:
> **[case-study]**
> Vista is a restaurant chain with 120 restaurants across Spain and Portugal. It serves traditional Mediterranean food to both local customers and tourists. Vista prides itself on providing a welcoming atmosphere and high-quality food. It employs around 800 staff, including chefs, waiters and managers.
> 
> In recent years the restaurant industry has become increasingly competitive, with many new restaurants opening across both countries. Vista has recently introduced a customer feedback system where diners are asked to rate their experience after each visit.

Analyse the importance of customer service quality to Vista.
parts.solutionMd:
High quality customer service is important to Vista because the restaurant industry in Spain and Portugal is very competitive** [1 mark]**. Customers who receive excellent service and food are more likely to return and leave positive reviews online **[1 mark]**, helping Vista to attract new customers and stand out from the many rival restaurants that have recently opened across both countries **[1 mark]**

Vista's customer feedback system also makes the quality of service particularly important **[1 mark]**. If customers leave negative feedback about slow service or poor food quality **[1 mark]**, this information could spread online and deter new customers from visiting, reducing Vista's bookings and putting pressure on its revenue **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying points about the importance of customer service quality to Vista.
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the points to Vista's context.
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the importance of quality to the business.
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Quality customer service is important to Vista because it serves both local customers and tourists **[1 mark]**. Tourists who enjoy an excellent experience may recommend Vista to others travelling to Spain and Portugal **[1 mark]**, generating valuable word-of-mouth promotion that could bring in new customers without Vista needing to spend money on advertising **[1 mark]**
> - Maintaining consistent quality across all 120 restaurants is important to Vista **[1 mark]**. If service quality varies between different locations, customers may have a poor experience at one restaurant and decide not to return to any Vista branch **[1 mark]**, damaging the overall brand reputation that Vista has worked hard to build across Spain and Portugal **[1 mark]**
> 
> Answers that list six points about customer service quality with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark.
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone.

parts.problemMd:
> **[case-study]**
> *TUI *is a holiday business that has over 100 years of experience. It offers customers a variety of holidays including staying in hotels, and river and ocean-going cruises. There are many extras that it offers to holiday makers including: car hire, extensions to the holiday and arranging day trips at all its holiday destinations.
> 
> The business is well known and flies its customers to over 180 destinations around the world, including Greece, Turkey and Spain. It has 1,600 travel agencies and 27 million customers. Holidays can be booked by visiting a travel agency or online.
> 
> *TUI *has holidays to meet the needs of all its customers: families, children, couples and those with disabilities.

Evaluate the benefits for *TUI *of providing a quality service. You should use the information provided as well as your own knowledge of business.
parts.solutionMd:
Quality service means consistently meeting or exceeding customer expectations to deliver a positive experience** [K]**

Providing a quality service is very important to TUI because it has 27 million customers who expect a high standard **[K] **across all of its holidays **[Ap]**. Customers who have a positive experience are more likely to book with TUI again, and with 1,600 travel agencies as well as online booking available **[Ap]**, satisfied customers can also help attract new bookings by recommending TUI to friends and family **[An]**

However, maintaining consistent quality across 180 destinations and 1,600 travel agencies is a significant challenge for TUI **[K]**. With such a large and complex operation **[Ap]**, it can be difficult to ensure every customer receives the same standard of service, particularly as TUI relies on hotels and local tour operators to deliver parts of the holiday experience **[An]**, meaning some aspects of quality may be harder for TUI to control directly **[E]**

Overall, providing a quality service is extremely important to TUI **[E]**. With over 100 years of experience and 27 million customers **[Ap]**, TUI's reputation is one of its most valuable assets **[An]**. Any significant decline in service quality could lead to negative online reviews that damage bookings across all of its destinations, which would be far more costly than the investment needed to maintain high standards **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - **12-mark 'evaluate' questions are marked using a level-of-response grid (L1 - L3)**
> - Examiners judge how well the response demonstrates:
> 
>   - Accurate knowledge of relevant business concepts and terminology
>   - Application of ideas to the case study throughout the answer
>   - Logical chains of reasoning explaining business impacts linking points together to show clear cause and effect
>   - A clear, justified conclusion based on evaluation of the issues
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - TUI serves a wide variety of customers including families, children, couples and those with disabilities → each group has different needs that must be met to deliver a quality experience → meaning TUI must train its staff carefully to cater for all groups effectively, ensuring every customer is satisfied and likely to rebook
> - With 27 million customers sharing their experiences online and through word of mouth → positive reviews of TUI's quality service can attract new customers at little additional cost → helping TUI to grow its bookings and compete effectively against other large holiday companies in a competitive market
> - Maintaining quality across 1,600 travel agencies and 180 destinations worldwide is expensive → TUI must invest heavily in staff training and monitoring standards across many different locations → meaning the cost of maintaining quality is high, but the reputational damage from poor service would be even more costly for a business that has spent over 100 years building its brand

parts.problemMd:
> **[case-study]**
> *Saha *is a small business in Türkiye (formerly known as Turkey) that opened in 2020 with 15 employees. It designs and manufactures robots, which are used in hospitals, hotels, and restaurants. In hospitals, its robots are used to move medical supplies between departments. In hotels and restaurants, the robots are used to welcome customers as they arrive and deliver food and drinks to hotel rooms and restaurant tables. *Saha *provides seven-day-a-week customer service for all businesses buying its robots.
> 
> Many new businesses are entering the global robot market and are competing for market share. Competitors in Türkiye include *NIO, Zoox *and *Vention*.
> 
> *Saha *has ambitious growth plans and has started to design robots that will be used in the home to help people with cleaning, shopping, security and entertainment. It aims to become a multinational business within five years to manufacture robots on all continents of the world.

*Saha *aims to manufacture robots that are high quality and long-lasting.

Evaluate the effects on *Saha *of introducing total quality management (TQM) to its business. You should use the information provided as well as your own knowledge of business.
parts.solutionMd:
Total quality management means every worker in a business is responsible for maintaining quality at every stage of production **[K]**

Introducing TQM could greatly benefit Saha because it aims to manufacture robots that are high quality and long-lasting **[K]**. If every one of Saha's 15 employees takes responsibility for quality during the design and manufacturing process, fewer faulty robots would reach customers in hospitals, hotels and restaurants** [Ap]**, helping Saha to build a strong reputation in a competitive market where rivals such as NIO, Zoox and Vention are fighting for the same customers **[An]**

However, introducing TQM could be challenging for a small business like Saha **[K]**. With only 15 employees **[Ap]**, training all staff to fully understand and apply TQM principles takes time and money that a small, recently opened business may not easily afford **[An]**, meaning the short-term costs of introducing TQM could put pressure on Saha's finances **[E]**

Overall, TQM is likely to be very beneficial for Saha in the long term **[E]**. As Saha plans to become a multinational business manufacturing robots on all continents **[Ap]**, building a culture of quality from an early stage with its small team will make it much easier to maintain high standards as the business grows **[An]**. The cost of introducing TQM now is likely to be far less than the damage caused by faulty robots reaching hospitals or other customers in the future **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - **12-mark 'evaluate' questions are marked using a level-of-response grid (L1 - L3)**
> - Examiners judge how well the response demonstrates:
>

>   - Application of ideas to the case study throughout the answer
>   - Logical chains of reasoning explaining business impacts linking points together to show clear cause and effect
>   - A clear, justified conclusion based on evaluation of the issues
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Saha provides a seven day a week customer service to all businesses buying its robots → TQM would help ensure robots are consistently reliable and require less after-sales support → reducing the cost of customer service and freeing up Saha's small team to focus on designing its new home robot range
> - TQM encourages all workers to take pride in the quality of their work → for a small team of 15 employees this could improve motivation and reduce the number of manufacturing errors → helping Saha to produce more reliable robots and reduce the cost of reworking or replacing faulty units
> - Saha has ambitious plans to manufacture robots in all continents within five years → introducing TQM now while the business is small makes it easier to embed a quality culture before the business grows → meaning quality standards are more likely to be maintained consistently as Saha expands into new international markets

parts.problemMd:
> **[case-study]**
> The *LEGO *Group is a privately-owned business in Denmark. The business was founded in 1932 by the Kristiansen family. The family still owns it. The name *LEGO *is an abbreviation of two Danish words, ‘leg godt’ which means ‘play well’. It is now one of the world’s largest manufacturers of toys with 15 factories and over 18,000 employees around the world.
> 
> *LEGO *manufactures toys, games and art materials for boys and girls of all ages, and products from films such as Star Wars and Harry Potter. It believes that children are the role models of the future and playing with *LEGO *can support children in a developing and complex world.

*LEGO *has progressed from a small carpenter’s shop to a global enterprise and has been named ‘Toy of the Century’ twice.

Evaluate how *LEGO *has maintained a competitive advantage in the making of toys and games. You should use the information provided as well as your own knowledge of business.
parts.solutionMd:
Competitive advantage means the features of a business that allow it to outperform its rivals and attract more customers** [K]**

One key reason LEGO has maintained competitive advantage is its strong and trusted brand identity **[K]**. Having been founded in 1932 and remaining family-owned by the Kristiansen family for over 90 years **[Ap]**, LEGO has built a reputation for quality and consistency that few toy manufacturers can match **[An]**. Its partnerships with major film franchises such as Star Wars and Harry Potter **[Ap]** allow LEGO to appeal to children and adults across different generations, meaning it can continuously attract new customers while retaining loyal ones **[An]**

However, maintaining competitive advantage in the toy industry is increasingly difficult **[K]**. As digital entertainment and electronic toys become more popular, traditional physical toys like LEGO face growing competition from technology-based alternatives **[An]**. With over 18,000 employees and 15 factories **[Ap]**, LEGO also carries very high fixed costs, which could reduce its ability to cut prices or invest quickly in new products if consumer tastes shift away from building toys **[An]**

Overall, LEGO is likely to maintain its competitive advantage in the long term **[E]**. Being named "Toy of the Century" twice **[Ap]** demonstrates that LEGO has successfully adapted to changing markets over decades without losing its core identity **[An]**. Its combination of a globally recognised brand, licensed products and a mission tied to child development gives it a unique position that rivals would find very difficult to replicate **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - **12-mark 'evaluate' questions are marked using a level-of-response grid (L1 - L3)**
> - Examiners judge how well the response demonstrates:
> 
>   - Accurate knowledge of relevant business concepts and terminology
>   - Application of ideas to the case study throughout the answer
>   - Logical chains of reasoning explaining business impacts linking points together to show clear cause and effect
>   - A clear, justified conclusion based on evaluation of the issues
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - LEGO manufactures toys and games for boys and girls of all ages → this broad product range means LEGO can appeal to a much wider market than competitors who target a narrower audience → allowing LEGO to generate higher revenue and invest more in new product development than smaller rivals
> - LEGO believes children are role models of the future and links its products to child development → this strong brand purpose builds emotional loyalty among parents who see LEGO as educational as well as entertaining → making parents more likely to choose LEGO over cheaper alternatives from competitors
> - LEGO has grown from a small carpenter's shop to a global enterprise with 15 factories → this scale gives LEGO significant purchasing and technical economies of scale → reducing its average costs and allowing it to price competitively while still maintaining profit margins that rivals with fewer factories cannot match

parts.problemMd:
> **[case-study]**
> *NEXT *is a well-known clothing retailer that operates in 70 countries and employs over 43,000 employees. Since *NEXT *commenced trading it has introduced many other products to its range such as home interiors, flowers and a wedding list service.
> 
> In 1999 *NEXT *launched its own online shopping platform, enabling customers to purchase its products where ever they live. It continues to improve its customer service by introducing new initiatives such as next day delivery.
> 
> *NEXT *mainly uses its own factories for production. However, it does purchase some clothes such as ladies dresses from Turkish factories.

*NEXT *continually monitors progress so that it can measure the success of its business. It aims to do this through improving manufacturing techniques and cutting costs, whilst still maintaining the quality of the goods produced.

Evaluate the importance for *NEXT *of maintaining quality throughout all of its manufacturing processes. You should use the information provided as well as your own knowledge of business.
parts.solutionMd:
Quality in manufacturing means producing goods that meet the standards customers expect, without defects or failures **[K]**

Maintaining quality is extremely important for NEXT because it operates in 70 countries and serves millions of customers **[Ap]**. If quality falls in any part of its manufacturing process, whether in its own factories or in Turkish factories producing ladies dresses **[Ap]**, faulty or poorly made products could reach customers worldwide** [K]**, damaging NEXT's reputation and leading to costly product returns that undermine its next day delivery service **[An]**. For a business that has expanded well beyond clothing into home interiors, flowers and wedding services **[Ap]**, consistent quality across all product lines is essential to retain customer loyalty in a highly competitive retail market **[An]**

However, NEXT's aim to cut costs whilst maintaining quality creates a genuine tension** [K]**. Reducing costs in manufacturing often puts pressure on the materials or processes used, and when some production is outsourced to external Turkish factories **[Ap]**, NEXT has less direct control over quality standards **[An]**, increasing the risk that substandard products reach its customers** [E]**

Overall, maintaining quality is one of the most important priorities for NEXT** [E]**. As a global retailer with over 43,000 employees and a well-established brand **[Ap]**, the reputational damage from poor quality goods would be far more costly than any short-term savings made by cutting manufacturing standards **[An]**. Investing in quality now protects the long-term profitability and customer trust that NEXT has built since 1999** [E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - **12-mark 'evaluate' questions are marked using a level-of-response grid (L1 - L3)**
> - Examiners judge how well the response demonstrates:
> 
>   - Accurate knowledge of relevant business concepts and terminology
>   - Application of ideas to the case study throughout the answer
>   - Logical chains of reasoning explaining business impacts linking points together to show clear cause and effect
>   - A clear, justified conclusion based on evaluation of the issues
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - NEXT continually monitors progress to measure the success of its business → maintaining quality throughout manufacturing gives NEXT reliable data on production performance → allowing managers to identify and fix problems before they affect customers, reducing waste and keeping average costs low
> - NEXT launched its online shopping platform in 1999 and has since introduced next day delivery → customers ordering online expect their goods to arrive quickly and in perfect condition → if quality control fails and faulty goods are delivered, the cost of returns and replacements would significantly increase NEXT's operating costs and reduce customer satisfaction
> - NEXT uses mainly its own factories for production → this gives NEXT greater control over quality standards compared to retailers that rely entirely on outsourcing → meaning NEXT is better placed than many competitors to identify quality problems early and make improvements to its manufacturing techniques
